summary: @servicetitan/unit-tests preinstall drops Bun runtime and executes obfuscated 727KB payload
details: The package declares `scripts.preinstall = "node setup.mjs"`. On `npm install`, setup.mjs probes for a system `bun` binary and, if absent, downloads the Bun runtime from `github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v<V>/...zip`, chmods it executable, and then invokes `execFileSync(bunBinary, ['math_init.js'], { stdio: 'inherit', cwd: D })`. The `math_init.js` file adjacent to setup.mjs is a 727KB Bun-compiled bundle (`// @bun @bun-cjs`) using string-array rotation obfuscation (a `WV8StW` shift routine over a large `n7gIxM` numeric/string array, `_0x`-style identifiers) with URL- and email-shaped fragments hidden across the string array; its behavior is not statically inspectable and only executes under the freshly dropped Bun runtime, evading Node-based scanners. The package impersonates ServiceTitan's private npm scope: name is `@servicetitan/unit-tests`, `description` is empty, the repository field points at `servicetitan/playground.git`, and the README is titled `uikit · Frontend Platform monorepo` — content unrelated to a `unit-tests` helper. `dist/index.js` is a small shim that re-exports `ts-mockito`, providing benign cover while the actual install-time behavior lives in the preinstall alternate-runtime dropper. The combined shape — namespace-hijack of a private vendor scope, mismatched README, benign shim as the documented entry point, and a preinstall step that fetches a second language runtime solely to execute an opaque bundled payload — is the alternate-runtime dropper pattern executed on default `npm install`.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
